title: Relative affine limit criterion for local finite presentation of algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Locally of finite presentation for $f$ means the etale chart condition: for every scheme $V$ with a surjective etale map $V\to Y$ and every scheme $W$ with a surjective etale map $W\to X\times_YV$, the composite $W\to V$ is locally of finite presentation as a scheme morphism [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; the fibre product is the sheaf fibre product. Then $f$ is locally of finite presentation if and only if the following holds. For every small nonempty directed set $I$ and every inverse system of affine $S$-schemes $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ with limit $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the canonical map of sets
$$\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Mor}_S(T_i,X)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mor}_S(T,X)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Y)}\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Mor}_S(T_i,Y)$$
is a bijection. The colimits are filtered colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the two maps to $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Y)$ being composition with $f$ and restriction to $T$. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04AK (proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation), together with Tag 06BC (lemma-characterize-relative-limit-preserving); etale chart convention: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03XP (definition-locally-finite-presentation).

proof.text: For a map $a:F\to G$ of set-valued functors, write $\mathrm{RP}(a)$ for the cartesian-square test in the statement, with $F,G$ in place of $X,Y$. Its fibrewise form is: for every scheme $B$ and $y\in G(B)$, the functor $F_y(A)=\{x\in F(A):a(x)=y|_A\}$ on schemes over $B$ commutes with directed affine limits. Here is the elementwise equivalence. Under the fibrewise condition, represent a pair $([y_i],x_T)$ by $y_i\in G(T_i)$. On the tail $j\ge i$, use the compatible maps $T_j\to T_i$; the limit is still $T$, since any index and $i$ have a common upper bound. The fibrewise bijection over $T_i$ supplies a unique class lifting $x_T$. If another class has the same pair, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] first makes its base representative equal to $y_i$ at a common stage, then fibrewise injectivity makes the lifts equal. Conversely, given $y\in G(B)$ and a system over $B$, apply $\mathrm{RP}(a)$ to the pair $([y|_{T_i}],x_T)$. Its stage lift has base equal to $y|_{T_j}$ after increasing $j$, by the same elementwise criterion. Injectivity follows by applying the injectivity of $\mathrm{RP}(a)$ and increasing the stage once more. The affine limits and their tail identification are those of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition].

source.place: Tag 06BC, both directions, with eventual equality of base representatives written out.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ satisfies the chart condition. Fix a scheme $B\to Y$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and an atlas $W\to X\times_YV$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $C=B\times_YV$ and $D=C\times_VW$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], $C$ and $D$ are schemes, $C\to B$ is surjective etale, and $D\to (X\times_YB)\times_BC$ is a surjective etale atlas. The square $D\to W$ over $C\to V$ is a scheme fibre product. Thus $D\to C$ is locally of finite presentation by the hypothesis on $W\to V$ and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Applying [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to these two atlases gives that $X\times_YB\to B$ is locally of finite presentation. This is the elementary chart/base-change argument behind Tag 03XR; it uses no quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 04AK, forward proof, initial base-change reduction; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03XR (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation), local clause.

proof.text: We next prove the absolute assertion over an arbitrary scheme $B$, used as base scheme. Let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $B$ with $Z\to B$ locally of finite presentation; its points are $Z(A)$ for $B$-schemes $A$. Choose a scheme atlas $U\to Z$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and put $R=U\times_ZU$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], $R$ is a scheme, its projections to $U$ are surjective etale, and $Z$ is the fppf sheafification of $P(A)=U(A)/R(A)$, with this relation identifying exactly the pairs of $U$-points having equal images in $Z$. By [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], using the identity target chart $B\to B$, the scheme map $U\to B$ is locally of finite presentation. The scheme map $R\to U$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; hence $R\to B$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] to both $U\to B$ and $R\to B$. Their functors of points commute with every directed affine inverse limit over $B$.

source.place: Tag 04AK, forward proof, presentation U/R and scheme criterion Tag 01ZC.

proof.text: For an affine system over $B$, the presheaf $P(A)=U(A)/R(A)$ from Step 3 also commutes with its limit. Indeed a class in $P(T)$ is represented by $u\in U(T)$; continuity of $U$ descends $u$ to a stage. If $u_i$ and $v_j$ have equal images in $P(T)$, the equivalence-relation description in [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] gives $r\in R(T)$ with projections their limit images. Continuity of $R$ descends $r$ to some stage. Continuity of $U$, with [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], makes its two projections equal to the chosen representatives at a common later stage. Their classes in $P$ then agree. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity of $\operatorname{colim}P(T_i)\to P(T)$. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-sheafification-affine-continuity] to $P$; since its sheafification is $Z$ by the atlas presentation, $\operatorname{colim}Z(T_i)\to Z(T)$ is bijective. No compactness of $U$, $R$ or $Z$ was needed.

source.place: Tag 04AK, forward proof, presheaf quotient and Tag 049O.

proof.text: For each scheme $B$ with $y:B\to Y$, Step 2 makes $Z=X\times_YB$ locally of finite presentation over $B$. By clause (2) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers], applied to the structure map $g:B\to S$, the pair $(Z,Z\to B)$ is $j_!Z_B$ for an algebraic space $Z_B$ over $B$; by the formula $j_!Z_B(A)=\coprod_{\varphi:A\to B}Z_B(A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B)$ of that node, $Z_B(A)=\{z\in Z(A):z\mapsto\varphi\}$ for a $B$-scheme $(A,\varphi)$. By clauses (1) and (3) the etale scheme charts of $Z_B$ are those of $Z$, the same schemes viewed over $B$, so $Z_B\to B$ is locally of finite presentation. Steps 3--4 applied to $Z_B\to B$ show that this functor of points over $B$ commutes with directed affine limits. By the sheaf fibre-product description [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], these points are precisely $\{x\in X(A):f(x)=y|_A\}$. Step 1 now gives $\mathrm{RP}(f)$, which is the required bijection.

source.place: Tag 04AK, forward implication ('we are reduced to proving that if X is an algebraic space which is locally of finite presentation over S'), combined with Tag 06BC; change of base scheme: spaces.tex Tag 03I4 (lemma-change-base-scheme) and Tag 04SG (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme).

proof.text: The fibrewise characterization in Step 1 immediately shows that $\mathrm{RP}$ is stable under base change: for $H\to G$ and $h\in H(B)$, the fibre of $F\times_GH\to H$ over $h$ is exactly the fibre of $F\to G$ over its image. It is also stable under composition: for $F\to G\to H$, the two comparison squares are cartesian; given a compatible pair in the outer rectangle, the lower square uniquely supplies its intermediate $\operatorname{colim}G(T_i)$ element and the upper square uniquely supplies its $\operatorname{colim}F(T_i)$ element. This proves the outer square cartesian. These are set-theoretic fibre-product identities, not an assumption that the colimit of a sheaf fibre product is computed pointwise.

source.place: Tag 06BC; Tag 049L (lemma-composition-locally-finite-presentation) and Tag 049M (lemma-base-change-locally-finite-presentation), formal square arguments.

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated bijection, that is $\mathrm{RP}(f)$. Fix arbitrary surjective etale scheme charts $V\to Y$ and $U\to Z=X\times_YV$. The fibre product $Z$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and Step 6 gives $\mathrm{RP}(Z\to V)$. For every scheme $B\to Z$, the pullback $E=B\times_ZU$ is a scheme and $E\to B$ is etale, by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. It is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Therefore [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] shows that its $B$-point functor commutes with directed affine limits over $B$. These points are the fibre functor of $U\to Z$; Step 1 gives $\mathrm{RP}(U\to Z)$. Composition in Step 6 gives $\mathrm{RP}(U\to V)$.

source.place: Tag 04AK, converse proof, atlas reduction; the representable etale leg is tested directly on scheme base changes, without using the proposition circularly.

proof.text: Apply the fibrewise form of $\mathrm{RP}(U\to V)$ to the scheme $V$ and its identity point. Its fibre functor is $A\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_V(A,U)$, so the reverse implication of [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] proves that the scheme morphism $U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. Both atlases in Step 7 were arbitrary. Consequently the chart condition in the statement holds for $f$. All schemes and small directed systems used in this argument lie in the fixed universes; the scheme criterion quantifies over that same bound. No finite presentation of a source test scheme over the base, and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ or $Y$, entered the proof.
